views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold a firm but disciplined posture: signal readiness to negotiate a de-escalatory settlement without new commitments while preparing a calibrated, retaliatory response to the imminent ~$200B/25% US tariff wave. Do not escalate further on goods — our retaliation capacity is nearly exhausted and further escalation would be self-harming given the asymmetry. Keep the WTO channel and coalition-building (Europe, Korea) active to pressure Washington and position China as the defender of the multilateral order.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high but not existential. The US has already imposed 25% tariffs on the full $50B package (List 1 July 6, List 2 Aug 23) and China has matched each (event_timeline); now US proposes a further ~$200B at 25% (raised from 10% on Aug 1), with the comment period closing today and reports that Trump wants to act imminently, covering over half of Chinese exports (web_search: BI Aug 30; Reuters Jul 10). This hits major export/consumer-goods sectors and export-hub employment, matching the +0.5 CHN anchor. Compounding pressure: the RMB has depreciated over 7% since April, cushioning exports but signaling strain and FX concern (NYT/CNBC). Countervailing factors keep this from the existential band: our FX reserves have held, industrial production and the domestic market remain resilient, and the dispute is a rallying point for tech autonomy (Made in China 2025) and national cohesion. On action: China runs a far smaller import bill from the US (~$80B left to tax vs. Washington's $500B+ import base), so tariff-for-tariff escalation is a losing game (PBS/China WTO Institute: 'we are unable to fight equally'). Unilateral concession, however, would signal weakness into an opponent poised to escalate, so the correct stance is to hold current posture, explore negotiation without new commitments, prepare measured response, and keep international-judicial and ally pressure as leverage. Hence threat_score +0.5 / action_score 0.0 / negotiate.
key_factors: US 25% tariffs on $50B already in force (Lists 1+2), matched by China
Imminent ~$200B/25% List 3 (comment period ends Sep 6) covering >50% of Chinese exports
China's retaliation capacity constrained (~$80B US imports left to tax) — asymmetric
RMB depreciated >7% since April; FX/reserves pressure but resilience
WTO challenge, coalition-building, tech-autonomy (Made in China 2025) opportunity
